## About

Ledger Row builds scheduling software for medical clinics.

We started in 2019 because a friend who runs a three-provider family practice in Tacoma kept losing Thursdays. Not to patients. To the phone — confirming, rescheduling, calling back the people who'd been bumped when a provider called in sick, then re-doing the whole board by hand on a whiteboard that nobody outside the front desk could see.

That's the problem we work on. Not clinic management in general, not billing, not charting. Scheduling.

The distinction matters, because most software sold to clinics tries to be everything and ends up being adequate at each piece. We'd rather do one thing properly. Our system handles provider templates, room and equipment constraints, recurring visit series, and the messy part nobody demos: what happens when someone cancels at 7 a.m. and you have a waitlist of forty-one people, half of whom can't come before noon.

We're a team of eleven, based in Seattle, and four of us have worked front-desk or practice-management jobs. We answer our own support line. When a clinic tells us a workflow is broken, the person who wrote that code usually hears about it the same day.

We're HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 Type II audited, and we'll send you the report before you ask.

About 340 clinics use Ledger Row today, most of them independent practices with two to twenty providers. If that's you, we'd like to hear what your Thursdays look like.
